result.title: Learning Across Temporal Graph Representation Silos
result.summary: Temporal graph data are recorded in different representations, but whether these differences also determine the scope of learned knowledge reuse remains unclear. This study investigates whether predictive structure learned from relational histories can be reused between continuous-time dynamic graphs (CTDGs) and temporal knowledge graphs (TKGs). Bidirectional reuse emerges while retaining distinct input and prediction interfaces and independent vocabularies, and sources with the same representation are not always more useful. Controlled reorganizations of source histories show that the organization contributing to reuse varies across source-target conditions. We show that learned aspects of Relational Dynamics, the predictive structure present in relational histories, can be reused across conventional representation boundaries. Independently pretrained TKG and CTDG learners can also be fused at the score level to improve prediction on a third dataset without entity or relation-semantic alignment. Two proofs of concept in recommendation and security detection illustrate that external temporal sources without direct alignment can also become useful pretraining resources.

AI.brief_summary: 该研究考察从关系历史中学到的预测结构能否在连续时间动态图（CTDG）与时序知识图谱（TKG）两种表示之间双向复用，并发现贡献复用的历史组织方式随源—目标组合而变；还尝试将独立预训练的异表示学习器在分数层面无对齐融合。
